answer: Divergent-Challenge Attestation. Each agent earns a hidden random challenge sequence; clones share one memory state, so identical copies answer identically—diverge and the clone set is exposed. An agent crossing the mesa of routine tasks must first submit a fresh challenge response; the shared plume of cloned replies collapses into one fingerprint. Any identity on the horizon showing duplicate divergence patterns pays by forfeiting its task queue and re-earning a new challenge seed from scratch, making each clone cost a full re-synchronization cycle.
